name: National Shrine of the Little Flower
history: The parish was founded in 1925 in a largely Protestant area, and its first wooden church was built in 1926. Its new building was paid for by the radio ministry of the pastor, Father Charles Coughlin, who broadcast from the tower in the 1930s; his politics later made him notorious, and the church was raided by the FBI in 1942. The tower was finished in 1931 and the church in 1936. Pope Francis named it a basilica in 2015.
arch: Lavish zig-zag Art Deco in granite and limestone. The octagonal nave seats 3,000 on two levels around a central altar.
features: The Charity Crucifixion Tower carries a 28-foot carved Christ on the cross, designed by René Paul Chambellan and carved by Enrico Liva.
It was built as a response to the Ku Klux Klan: a "cross they could not burn".

look.d: Carved into the limestone tower facing Woodward Avenue.
The symbols of the Four Evangelists mark its upper corners.

fun: The first wooden church burned on 17 March 1936, just as the new building was being completed.
journal: Art Deco faith on Woodward Avenue. A stone cross no one could burn.

quiz.q: What is the tower's carving called a response to?
a: The Ku Klux Klan's cross burnings
